mathematics.logical_review: The current manuscript contains complete proofs of the broad-Q Koszul/index/seven-period results, the domain structure and z-regularity criterion, the pure-jump-one dichotomy and exclusion of its finite-width branch, the finite Ore indexed-isomorphism criterion, and the complete diagonal indexed quotient. Independent AI-assisted readings checked the new tensor-chain and monodromy arguments, the noncircular use of AS assumptions, the indexed matrix and scalar recurrences, both parity conditions for the derivation, and all exceptional diagonal parameters. These readings are neither formal verification nor external peer review.
mathematics.scope: Over the standing algebraically closed field of characteristic zero: all Q for the outer relation dimensions r_2=r_5=1 and pure-jump-one Hilbert function n+1; all valid domain Ore data for the finite necessary-and-sufficient indexed-isomorphism criterion; all nonzero parameters of the diagonal quantum family for its involution quotient. The domain structure theorem still does not prove that every Q object is a domain. General n retains the existing hypotheses, except that the stated finite isomorphism criterion also applies within the specified quadratic Ore family.

exact_computation.new_results: The new theorems have analytic proofs. Integer recurrence and monodromy calculations reproduce a numerical obstruction that the tensor-chain proof excludes; the computation does not certify an AS algebra.
